leadRulings.question: capability spec §6: whether the 5-point non-inferiority margin (J, L) is right for n = 90
leadRulings.ruling: option (c): keep the 5-point non-inferiority margin at n = 90 tasks and pre-register k = 2 repeats per task per arm; the same margin rule applies to track L
leadRulings.condition: estimate the VM-hours J needs at k = 2 before freezing (vmHoursEstimate); if that would delay the R1 pilot, the hcu+shell head-to-head, the corrections A/B or the 90 s demo, switch to option (b), a 7-point margin at k = 1, before freezing and never after any data

vmHoursEstimate.basis: measured M1 figures on the single Windows VM (docs/baseline/screenshot-agent.md, budget): cold reset 140 s + redeploy ~100 s + trial ~135 s = 375 s per trial, one reset per trial; the Ultra trial time is not measured yet
vmHoursEstimate.trackL: track L runs on the Linux path (spec §2 L), not the Windows VM; its estimate belongs to L's own pre-registration
vmHoursEstimate.criticalPath: Spec §4 and m2-plan §7.0 give a capability track VM time only when the critical path does not need the VM, and J's Windows arm also waits for the guest-side router (fast-path.md §6). Run that way, J's VM-hours come after and around the R1 pilot, the hcu+shell head-to-head, the corrections A/B and the 90 s demo and do not delay them, so option (c) applies. If the coordinator's VM schedule shows otherwise before this pre-registration is frozen, j-v1 switches to option (b) before freezing.
